change_evidence.pre_simplification_verdict: FAIL: WP-015 returned a valid failed wreq product-candidate verdict; no shipped ordinary transport dependency was authorized; current validation forbids all product-native exceptions; the proposed reqwest rustls label would hide AWS-LC unless default features and crypto provider are explicitly controlled; and ring's packaged pregenerated Windows assembly objects were not yet explicit or governed.
simplification_changes: Kept the approved ordinary transport in the existing prerequisite-only fforager-transport crate instead of creating a product crate or a second policy model.
Bound rustls to ring and webpki-roots in one provider-owned ClientConfig, avoiding process-global provider state and runtime platform trust selection.
Separated ordinary-transport and wreq-adjudication Cargo features so the default ordinary graph does not compile or resolve the browser engine.
Reused the authenticated local protocol harness for proxy, redirect, retry, cookie, decompression, and worker-lifecycle proof instead of adding external-network fixtures.
change_evidence.post_simplification_verdict: PASS: the narrow prerequisite implementation preserves the exact approved dependency boundary, fail-closed browser refusal, Ferric-owned control ceiling, and zero product progress while removing hidden provider, source, native-artifact, and worker-lifecycle ambiguity.

COUNTERFACTUAL_CHECKS: Adding a reqwest resolved feature changes the exact feature surface and is rejected before the ordinary profile can pass.
Adding a synthetic root-reachable no-links FFI package and edge changes the complete closure and is rejected.
Substituting the reqwest extracted source root changes the registry source closure and is rejected.
Adding, removing, replacing, renaming, or nesting a packaged native object changes the recursive ring inventory and is rejected.
Changing governed archive bytes or source files including build.rs, crypto code, and Windows verification code changes the pinned digest and is rejected.
BOUNDARY_PROBES: An unreachable ambient proxy and authenticated local redirect prove proxy clearing and redirect refusal at the configured client-to-wire boundary.
A retryable local response proves the dependency retry service returns the first 503 without an automatic second attempt.
A reused client receives Set-Cookie and then contacts a second loopback origin whose captured request contains no Cookie header.
A gzip-framed response remains raw at byte observation, while the exact resolved feature graph provides the primary decompression-disable proof.
TLS-only, HTTP2-only, and combined browser-fingerprint demands return exact typed blockers before client construction or network execution.
NEGATIVE_PATH_CHECKS: A compression request or body failure drops and joins the local server and then joins the acknowledgement worker before returning.
Forged control evidence or a forged crypto-provider identity fails strict report reconstruction.
The ordinary component cannot emit PASS_ORDINARY_TRANSPORT_DECISION and records final_decision_verdict_emitted=false.
The ordinary feature profile resolves without wreq, BoringSSL, AWS-LC, native-tls, OpenSSL, or a silent browser fallback.
No reqwest or rustls ordinary implementation exists under product, so the prerequisite cannot be mistaken for shipped downloader behavior.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.finding: Cookie disabling was initially structural only; the final boundary probe now reuses one client across two loopback origins and proves no Cookie header is emitted.
Compression request failures could detach the acknowledgement worker; every failure path now drops and joins the server and explicitly joins the worker.
A top-level packaged-object inventory could miss nested or renamed native artifacts; recursive relative-path and byte hashing now rejects every tested mutation.
Manifest markers alone did not authenticate native package contents; Cargo.lock, cached archive bytes, and complete extracted source inventories are now digest checked.
Named native-link checks could miss an undeclared no-links FFI wrapper; the complete root-reachable identity, feature, and edge closure now fails on any added package or edge.
Exact graph identity did not detect arbitrary modified transitive source bytes; all 109 reachable registry source inventories now feed a separately pinned aggregate digest.

RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Public-certificate HTTPS and staged product-runtime behavior are intentionally outside this prerequisite and require the future fforager-net consumer plus FF-GATE-RUNTIME-001.
Ordinary reqwest transport does not provide browser TLS or HTTP2 fingerprints; those requests remain typed failures while wreq stays disabled and non-shipped.
Ferric-owned DNS provenance, SSRF enforcement, redirect approval, cookie persistence, pool partitioning, resource admission, retry budgets, and decompression limits remain future product work.
